q: The first Surah of the Glorious Qur'an is known as _____.
explanation: Surat Al-Fatihah is the opening chapter of the Qur'an and is essential in every unit of the Muslim prayer (Salat).

q: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) over a period of approximately _____ years.
explanation: The revelation began when the Prophet was 40 and ended shortly before his death at 63, totaling 23 years (13 in Makkah and 10 in Madinah).

q: The primary source of Islamic Law (Shari'ah) is the _____.
explanation: The Qur'an is the ultimate and most authoritative source of guidance in Islam, followed by the Sunnah/Hadith.

q: A Hadith that is attributed directly to Allah but phrased by the Prophet (SAW) is called _____.
explanation: Hadith Qudsi (Sacred Hadith) contains meanings from Allah expressed in the Prophet's words, distinguished from the Qur'an which is Allah's literal word.

q: The 'Year of Elephant' (Amul-Fil) is significant in Islamic history because it was the year _____.
opts: the first battle of Islam occurred
explanation: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) was born in Makkah in 570 CE, the same year Abrahah attempted to destroy the Ka'bah with an army of elephants.

q: The term 'Tawhid' in Islam refers to the _____.
explanation: Tawhid is the core concept of monotheism in Islam, asserting that Allah is One and Unique in His essence and attributes.

q: Which of the following is NOT among the 'As-Sihah as-Sittah' (The Six Authentic Books of Hadith)?
explanation: Muwatta Malik is a highly respected collection but is not traditionally numbered among the 'Six Books' (Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi, Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah).

q: The first Caliph in Islam was _____.
explanation: Abu Bakr was elected as the leader of the Muslim community immediately after the death of the Prophet (SAW).

q: The migration of the early Muslims from Makkah to Abyssinia (Ethiopia) was to escape the persecution of the _____.
explanation: The Quraysh polytheists persecuted early converts, prompting the Prophet to advise some to seek refuge with the Christian King Negus (Najashi).

q: The ritual of 'Sa'y' during Hajj involves walking between the hills of _____.
explanation: Sa'y commemorates Hajar's (AS) search for water for her son Ismail (AS) between the hills of Safa and Marwa.

q: The amount of Zakat payable on wealth (gold/silver/cash) that has reached the Nisab is _____.
explanation: Zakat on liquid assets is calculated at 2.5% (one-fortieth) of the total value once held for a full lunar year.

q: The Surah that is equivalent to one-third of the Qur'an in terms of reward and meaning is _____.
explanation: Surat al-Ikhlas summarizes the concept of Tawhid, which is the foundation of one-third of the Qur'anic message.

q: In Islamic Inheritance (Mirath), a daughter's share when she is the only child is _____.
explanation: According to the Qur'an (Surat an-Nisa), if there is only one daughter and no son, she receives half of the estate.

q: The companion who was known as 'Dhul-Nurayn' (The possessor of two lights) was _____.
explanation: Uthman b. Affan was given this title because he married two of the Prophet's daughters, Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum.

q: The battle in which the Muslims suffered a setback due to the disobedience of the archers was the Battle of _____.
explanation: At Uhud, the archers left their positions on the hill against the Prophet's orders, allowing Khalid b. Walid to lead a counter-attack.

q: The science of the rules governing the correct pronunciation of the Qur'an is called _____.
explanation: Tajwid ensures that every letter of the Qur'an is pronounced correctly from its point of articulation with its proper characteristics.

q: The angel responsible for blowing the trumpet (Sur) to signal the Day of Judgment is _____.
explanation: Israfil is the angel tasked with blowing the trumpet twice: once to end life and once to initiate the resurrection.

q: The collection and compilation of the Qur'an into a single volume was initiated during the Caliphate of _____.
explanation: Following the Battle of Yamamah where many huffaz died, Abu Bakr ordered Zaid b. Thabit to compile the Qur'an into a single book (Mushaf).

q: A 'Mahr' in an Islamic marriage is the _____.
opts: obligatory gift from husband to wife
explanation: Mahr is the mandatory dowry or gift paid by the groom to the bride at the time of marriage as a token of respect and security.

q: The act of 'Tayammum' is performed when _____ is unavailable.
explanation: Tayammum is dry ablution using clean earth/sand when water is not available or its use is harmful to health.

content: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) said: 'None of you truly believes until he wishes for his brother what he wishes for himself.' (Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim)

questions.q: The central theme of this Hadith is _____.
questions.explanation: The Hadith emphasizes that true faith involves selfless love and wishing good for others as much as for oneself.
While it primarily addresses the brotherhood in faith, scholars interpret the spirit of the Hadith as universal kindness toward all fellow humans.

q: The 'Nisab' of cattle (cows) for Zakat starts at _____ animals.
explanation: Zakat is not due on cows until the owner has at least 30, at which point one one-year-old calf (Tabi') is due.

q: The term 'Shirk' means _____.
explanation: Shirk is the opposite of Tawhid and is considered the gravest sin in Islam, as it compromises the absolute oneness of God.

q: The 'Hijrah' calendar begins from the year the Prophet (SAW) migrated from _____ to _____.
explanation: The Islamic (Hijri) era marks the migration to Madinah in 622 CE, which established the first Islamic state.

q: The Surah that protects a person from the trials of the Dajjal (Anti-Christ) if the first ten verses are memorized is _____.
explanation: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) recommended reciting Surat al-Kahf on Fridays and memorizing its opening for protection against the Dajjal.

q: The 'Khulafah ar-Rashidun' refers to the _____.
explanation: This title is given to the first four Caliphs: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali, who followed the Sunnah of the Prophet closely.

q: The pre-Islamic period of ignorance in Arabia is known as _____.
explanation: Jahiliyyah refers to the state of affairs in Arabia before the mission of Prophet Muhammad (SAW), characterized by idolatry and tribal warfare.

q: The Prophet's wife who was the daughter of Abu Bakr and a great scholar of Hadith was _____.
explanation: Aishah (RA) was known for her intelligence and contributed significantly to the preservation and teaching of Islamic knowledge.

q: The 'Iddah' period for a divorced woman who is not pregnant is _____.
explanation: The Qur'an specifies three monthly cycles (Quru') for a divorced woman to ensure there is no pregnancy before she remarries.

q: The treaty signed between the Muslims and the Quraysh in 628 CE was the Treaty of _____.
explanation: Hudaibiyyah was a 10-year peace treaty that, although initially seeming disadvantageous to Muslims, led to the peaceful conquest of Makkah.

q: The first Mu'adhin (caller to prayer) in Islam was _____.
explanation: Bilal, a former slave from Ethiopia, was chosen for his beautiful and strong voice to call Muslims to prayer.

q: A prayer offered for a deceased Muslim before burial is called _____.
explanation: Salat al-Janazah is a funeral prayer consisting of four Takbirs, performed in congregation standing up (without Ruku' or Sujud).

q: The 'Night of Power' (Laylatul-Qadr) is better than _____ months.
explanation: Surat al-Qadr states that worship on this night in Ramadan is better than a thousand months of worship.

q: The legal ruling that is 'highly recommended' but not strictly obligatory is called _____.
explanation: Mustahabb actions are those for which a person is rewarded if performed, but not punished if omitted.

q: The Surah that warns against backbiting and slandering is _____.
explanation: Surat al-Humazah begins by condemning 'every slanderer and backbiter'.

q: The Islamic concept of 'Ihsan' means _____.
opts: to worship Allah as if you see Him
explanation: In the Hadith of Jibril, Ihsan is defined as 'to worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you cannot see Him, you know He sees you'.

q: Which Caliph oversaw the expansion of Islam into Persia, Egypt, and the Levant?
explanation: Umar (RA) was the great administrator and conqueror under whose rule the Islamic empire expanded most rapidly.

q: The 'Sunnah' refers to the _____ of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW).
explanation: Sunnah encompasses everything the Prophet said (Qawl), did (Fi'l), or tacitly approved (Taqrir).

q: The major theme of the 'Makkan' Surahs is usually _____.
explanation: Makkan Surahs focus on establishing faith, the oneness of Allah, and the reality of life after death, while Madinan Surahs focus on law and community building.

q: The number of Sajdah (prostration) marks found in the Qur'an is _____.
explanation: Most scholars agree on 14 specific verses in the Qur'an where it is Sunnah to perform a prostration (Sajdah at-Tilawah) upon recitation.

q: The 'Battle of the Trench' is also known as the Battle of _____.
explanation: It is called 'Al-Ahzab' because various tribes formed a confederacy to attack the Muslims in Madinah.

q: A Hadith that has a broken chain of narrators is classified as _____.
explanation: Munqati' refers to a Hadith where a narrator is missing from the chain of transmission.

q: The prophet mentioned most frequently by name in the Qur'an is _____.
explanation: Prophet Musa (AS) is mentioned 136 times in the Qur'an across many Surahs.

q: The direction (Qiblah) Muslims face during prayer was changed from _____ to Makkah.
explanation: Early in Madinah, the Qiblah was toward Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem before the revelation of Surat al-Baqarah verse 144.

q: The term 'Sadaqah' generally refers to _____.
explanation: While Zakat is obligatory, Sadaqah refers to any act of voluntary kindness or financial help given for the sake of Allah.

q: The 'Haram' months in which fighting is prohibited are _____.
explanation: These four months are sacred, and the Qur'an forbids initiating warfare during them.

q: The compiler of the most authentic book of Hadith, Sahih Al-Bukhari, was from _____.
explanation: Imam Muhammad b. Ismail al-Bukhari was born in Bukhara, in present-day Uzbekistan.

q: The act of 'Istighfar' means _____.
explanation: Istighfar is the act of saying 'Astaghfirullah' (I seek Allah's forgiveness).

q: A person who memorizes the entire Qur'an is called a _____.
explanation: Hafiz (Guardian) is the title for someone who has committed the 6,236 verses of the Qur'an to memory.

q: The 'Riddah' wars were fought during the Caliphate of Abu Bakr against _____.
explanation: After the Prophet's death, some tribes rebelled or followed false prophets like Musaylimah; Abu Bakr fought to maintain the unity of Islam.

q: The 'Takbirat al-Ihram' is the _____.
explanation: This Takbir signals the entry into the sacred state of prayer, during which ordinary actions like eating or talking become forbidden.

q: The 'Al-Faruq' was the title of which Caliph?
explanation: Umar was called Al-Faruq (The one who distinguishes between truth and falsehood) for his strict justice.

q: The main focus of Surat al-Ma'un is _____.
explanation: The Surah criticizes those who pray for show but refuse to help the orphans and the poor.

q: Islamic monotheism is divided into three categories: Tawhid ar-Rububiyyah, Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, and _____.
explanation: The third category involves the belief in Allah's unique Names and Attributes as mentioned in the Qur'an and Sunnah.

q: The 'Sujud as-Sahw' is performed when a person _____.
opts: makes a mistake or forgetfulness in prayer
explanation: Two extra prostrations are performed at the end of Salat to compensate for unintentional omissions or additions.

q: The primary objective of 'Sawm' (fasting) as stated in the Qur'an is to achieve _____.
explanation: Surat al-Baqarah 183 states: '...so that you may become God-fearing/righteous (Taqwa)'.

q: The collection of sayings and deeds of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) is called _____.
explanation: Hadith is the record of the Sunnah.

q: In Shari'ah, the prohibited acts are known as _____.
explanation: Haram refers to anything explicitly forbidden by Allah and His Messenger.

q: The first revelation came to the Prophet in the Cave of _____.
explanation: Mount Nur houses the Cave of Hira, where Angel Jibril first commanded the Prophet to 'Read!' (Iqra).

q: Which Caliph was known for his extreme modesty and for compiling the standard version of the Qur'an used today?
explanation: Uthman (RA) ordered the standardized 'Uthmanic Codex' to be sent to all major Islamic cities to ensure uniformity.

q: The 'Asadullah' (Lion of Allah) was a title of _____.
explanation: The Prophet's uncle, Hamzah, was given this title for his bravery, though Ali (RA) was also famously brave.

q: The Surah that must be recited in every Rak'ah of prayer is _____.
explanation: Prayer is invalid without the recitation of Al-Fatihah, known as 'Umm al-Kitab'.

q: A 'Mushrik' is a person who _____.
explanation: The term comes from 'Shirk', meaning polytheism or idolatry.

q: The Islamic term for the 'oneness of God' is _____.
explanation: Tawhid is the defining doctrine of Islam.

q: The five daily prayers are: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and _____.
explanation: Isha is the night prayer, the last of the five obligatory daily prayers.

q: The term 'Tafsir' refers to _____.
explanation: Mufassirun (commentators) use linguistics, history, and Hadith to explain the meanings of Qur'anic verses.

q: A Hadith narrated by only one person at every stage of the chain is called _____.
explanation: Gharib means 'strange' or 'solitary' in Hadith terminology.

q: The Prophet Muhammad (SAW) belonged to the tribe of _____.
explanation: He was from the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh tribe in Makkah.

q: The 'Kharaj' in Islamic taxation refers to _____.
explanation: Kharaj is a tax on agricultural land, typically applied to lands conquered by Muslims.

q: The Surah that describes the short duration of time and the importance of faith and good deeds is _____.
explanation: Surat al-Asr emphasizes that all mankind is in a state of loss except those who have faith, do good, and encourage truth and patience.
